deep.reconstruction:
The page is not a derivation. It is one sheet of a large hand-ruled table of quadratic residues among primes. This sheet is the 20th in red-crayon foliation and continues sheets 19 and 21.

Layout:
- Rows are the primes p = 439, 443, 449, 457, 461, 463, 467, 479, 487, 491, 499, 503, 509, 521, with 523 added in red ink.
- Columns are the 24 consecutive primes q from 661 to 827. The preceding sheet covers 509 to 659 and the next covers 829 to 997, so the full table runs to q < 1000.
- A small circle at (p, q) means that q is a quadratic residue mod p. In modern notation, the circle marks Legendre symbol (q/p) = +1.
- Circles in horizontally or vertically adjacent cells are joined by short strokes. This is a visual aid only, showing the pattern of runs or blocks. It carries no extra mathematical content that I can detect.

Verification (mine), red row p = 523:
- I computed (q/523) by reduction and reciprocity, using q - 523 and the small-prime characters mod 523: (2/523) = -1, (3/523) = -1, (5/523) = -1, (7/523) = +1, (11/523) = +1, (13/523) = +1, (17/523) = +1, (19/523) = +1, (23/523) = +1, (29/523) = +1, (31/523) = +1, (37/523) = -1, (41/523) = +1, (89/523) = +1, (137/523) = +1, (149/523) = +1.
- The residues found are exactly 661, 673, 683, 691, 709, 719, 739, 769, 773, 787, 827. These are precisely the red circles, so the row matches perfectly (11 of 24).

Other rows:
- Row 503 matches at every column I checked: 661, 673, 691, 701, 719, 727, 739, 761, 797, 811, 827 are residues, and 677, 683, 709 are not.
- Row 443 entries at 821 and 823 are correct.
- Row 439 has circles at 661, 673, 683, 691, 719, 743, 773, 811, 823. Using (2/439) = 1, (3/439) = -1, (5/439) = 1, (7/439) = 1, (13/439) = 1, (17/439) = -1, (61/439) = 1, (191/439) = 1, I find these circles agree with (q/439) except for two places, noted under errors.

Rows 509 and 521 are left blank. They are simply unfilled; about half their cells should be circled.

Purpose: this is an empirical table of the quadratic character of primes modulo primes. It is the kind of data Gauss collected in induction toward, and checking of, the reciprocity law, and it resembles an extended version of the residue table in the Disquisitiones (Tab. II).
errors: Row 439, column 727: no circle is drawn, but 727 = 439 + 288 = 439 + 2^5*3^2 and (2/439) = +1, so (727/439) = +1. This looks like an omission (or a reading problem in the image).

Row 439: a circle stands under 823 and none under 821. However (823/439) = (384/439) = (2/439)^7*(3/439) = -1, while (821/439) = (2*191/439) = +1. This is probably a one-column slip; I hedge because it depends on the image reading.
Rows 509 and 521 are entirely empty although each should contain roughly 12 residues. The table is incomplete rather than wrong.

results.what: Table marking which primes q in [661,827] are quadratic residues modulo the primes p in [439,523] (circle iff (q/p) = +1)
results.modern_name: Table of Legendre symbols / quadratic residue table for primes
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, Tab. II, a smaller table); such tables are standard number-theoretic computation

deep.surprise_reason: Extensive quadratic-residue tables used empirically for reciprocity are well documented for Gauss. This sheet is routine computational data, notable only for its size and the graphic device of linking adjacent entries.

checkable.asserts: Red row 523 lists exactly the column primes that are quadratic residues mod 523
727 is a residue mod 439 (circle missing in manuscript)
The circle under 823 in row 439 should be under 821
Row 443 entries at 821 and 823 are correct
Checked entries of row 503 agree with the quadratic character mod 503
